record.paper_title: On the combinatorics of tableaux -- A notebook of open problems
record.original_question: Can anything be said in general about the number of distinct monomials in the Schur functions λ(x1, . . . , xn) for arbitraryλ?

evidence.quote: [Stan1999, Ch. 7 Exer. 33(c)] Can anything be said in general about the number of distinct monomials in the Schur functions λ(x1, . . . , xn) for arbitraryλ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a partition $\lambda = (\lambda_1 \geq \lambda_2 \geq \cdots \geq \lambda_k > 0)$ and a positive integer $n$, let $s_\lambda(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ denote the Schur polynomial in $n$ variables, defined by
$$s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_n) \;=\; \sum_{T} x^{T},$$
where the sum is over all semistandard Young tableaux $T$ of shape $\lambda$ with entries from $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, and $x^{T} = x_1^{m_1(T)} x_2^{m_2(T)} \cdots x_n^{m_n(T)}$ with $m_i(T)$ the number of entries of $T$ equal to $i$. Equivalently,
$$s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_n) \;=\; \sum_{\mu} K_{\lambda\mu}\, x^{\mu},$$
where $\mu = (\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_n)$ ranges over weak compositions of $|\lambda|$ with at most $n$ parts and $K_{\lambda\mu}$ is the Kostka number.

Let $M(\lambda, n)$ denote the number of distinct monomials $x^\mu$ appearing with nonzero coefficient in $s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$; equivalently,
$$M(\lambda,n) \;=\; \#\bigl\{\mu \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^{n} : K_{\lambda\mu} > 0\bigr\}.$$

Determine, for arbitrary $\lambda$ and $n$, a useful general statement (closed-form formula, generating function, asymptotic estimate, or combinatorial characterization) for the quantity $M(\lambda, n)$.
artifact.status_search_result:
A web search did not surface a definitive published resolution of this question (Stanley, EC2, Exercise 7.33(c)). The number of distinct monomials in $s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ equals the number of compositions $\mu$ with positive Kostka number $K_{\lambda\mu}$, which is known to be the number of partitions $
u$ of $|\lambda|$ with $
u 	rianglelefteq \lambda$ and $\ell(
u)\le n$, multiplied/expanded over rearrangements, but no clean general closed form appears to be established. The status appears to remain unresolved in general.

status_evidence.title: Schur polynomial - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Schur polynomial $s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ is expressed as a sum over semistandard Young tableaux, with coefficients given by Kostka numbers $K_{\lambda\mu}$.
status_evidence.claim: Distinct monomials in $s_\lambda$ correspond to weights $\mu$ with $K_{\lambda\mu}>0$; no general closed form for their count is stated.

status_evidence.title: An introduction to Schur polynomials (Prasad)
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference describing the monomial expansion of Schur functions in terms of Kostka numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Survey-level treatments do not provide a general formula for the number of distinct monomials in $s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$.
